one_line: This ad uses a visual illusion and data visualization to show how chin position affects nose perception, promoting an AI facial preview tool.

hook.what_happens: A split-screen face is shown with the question of whether the viewer's nose is too big.
hook.why_it_works: It targets a common facial insecurity with a surprising visual paradox.

shots.description: Split-screen comparison of a woman's face with overlays showing chin augmentation and pixel changes.
Side-by-side comparison of the original and edited face.
Call to action screen with a search bar mockup.

devices.name: split-screen slider
devices.what_it_is: A vertical line dividing two states of the same face.

devices.name: pixel change heatmap
devices.what_it_is: A glowing overlay highlighting modified pixels.
devices.used_for: Proving which parts of the image actually changed.

devices.name: bar chart
devices.what_it_is: A simple bar graph showing percentage values.

devices.name: search bar mockup
devices.what_it_is: A simulated search engine input field.

onscreen_text.text: Same face. Same nose. Same woman, twice.
But it looks smaller in the second. Her chin is what moved.
Almost none of it is on her nose.
Your eye doesn't measure features. It compares them. When the chin sits back, the nose stands out.
Your brain calls it a big nose. Bring it forward and the nose has something to sit against. It didn't shrink. The face caught up.
Your nose just got smaller. You didn't touch it.
Not one feature. The whole face.
The question was never which feature to fix. It's what the whole face does when one thing moves.

transcript.text: Think your nose is too big? Same face, same nose, same woman, twice.
Same nose, both photographs, but it looks smaller in the second.
Here is every pixel that changed. Almost none of it is on her nose.
Your eye doesn't measure features, it compares them. When the chin sits back, the nose stands out.
Your brain calls it a big nose. Bring it forward and the nose has something to sit against. It didn't shrink, the face caught up.
Try it right now. Push your lower jaw forward, hold it there, watch your nose. Your nose just got smaller, you didn't touch it.
The question was never which feature to fix, it's what the whole face does when one thing moves.
See it on your own face first. A preview, not a promise. Search Refina AI.

narrative_arc: Present a visual paradox involving nose size.
Reveal that chin adjustment, not nose reduction, caused the change.
Provide data-driven proof of pixel changes.
Explain the psychological optical illusion of facial comparison.
Prompt the viewer to perform a physical test to experience the illusion.
Introduce the AI preview tool as the solution to test this on themselves.

cta.what: Search Refina AI to preview facial changes.

subjects: Unnamed female model demonstrating facial structure changes
what_makes_it_work: Leverages a compelling optical illusion to challenge user assumptions.
Uses data visualization to build scientific credibility.
Includes an immediate, interactive physical call-to-action that proves the concept.

animations.purpose: Compares before/after states of the face directly.
animations.reusable_as: Comparing any two states of an image (e.g., color grading, editing).

animations.name: ContourDraw
animations.what_moves: Oval outline around the chin and text labels
animations.purpose: Highlights the specific area of the face that was modified.
animations.reusable_as: Drawing attention to specific UI elements or product features.

animations.name: AnimatedBarChart
animations.purpose: Displays quantitative data of pixel changes per facial region.
animations.reusable_as: Showing statistics, performance metrics, or survey results.
animations.would_need_building: AnimatedBarChart with growing bars and counting labels

animations.name: AnimatedCheckList

animations.reusable_as: Displaying tutorials, feature lists, or onboarding steps.

animations.name: DivergePanels
animations.what_moves: Single portrait splitting into side-by-side comparison
animations.purpose: Shows the original and modified faces side-by-side for final comparison.
animations.reusable_as: Comparing two distinct variations of a product or design.
animations.would_need_building: DivergePanels to split and slide a single asset into two panels

animation_language_summary.how_things_enter: Elements fade or scale up smoothly in place.
animation_language_summary.how_things_leave: Elements fade out or are wiped away by transitions.
animation_language_summary.how_scenes_change: Hard cuts or slider wipes transition between scenes.
animation_language_summary.what_stays_still: The central portrait remains anchored throughout most of the video.
animation_language_summary.rhythm: Bursty, with moments of stillness followed by quick, informative transitions.

what_we_should_steal: DivergePanels for elegant side-by-side comparisons from a single asset source
AnimatedBarChart for clean, dynamic data visualization in short-form ads
